answer: One concrete mechanism: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because cedar only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, grove is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any yarrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
